fine_lines.title: how much vs how many
fine_lines.explanation_ar: how much مع الأسماء غير المعدودة (money, water, shrimp, seafood) ومع السعر. how many مع الأسماء المعدودة بصيغة الجمع (crabs, people, eggs).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Use how much with uncountable nouns (money, water, shrimp, seafood) and to ask about price. Use how many with plural countable nouns (crabs, people, eggs).

examples.sentence: How much money can you spend?
How much shrimp do you want?
How many crabs do you want?

fine_lines.title: cash vs credit
fine_lines.explanation_ar: cash = نقود ورقية ومعدنية. credit = الدفع ببطاقة الائتمان. سؤال الكاشير: Cash or credit?
fine_lines.explanation_en: Cash = coins and paper money. Credit = paying with a credit card. The cashier asks: Cash or credit?

examples.sentence: Can I pay by credit card?

fine_lines.title: sail vs sailor vs sailboat
fine_lines.explanation_ar: sail فعل = يُبحر (أو اسم = شراع). sailor = الشخص الذي يُبحر (بحّار). sailboat = المركب الشراعي.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Sail is the verb (or the cloth on a boat). A sailor is the person. A sailboat is the boat.

grammar.title: How much / How many
grammar.explanation_ar: للسؤال عن الكمية: How many + اسم معدود جمع (crabs, people). How much + اسم غير معدود (money, shrimp, water). وتُستخدم How much أيضاً للسؤال عن السعر: How much is it?
grammar.explanation_en: To ask about quantity: How many + plural countable noun (crabs, people). How much + uncountable noun (money, shrimp, water). We also use How much to ask about price: How much is it?
examples: How much money can you spend?
How much shrimp do you want?
How many crabs do you want?
How much do I need for five people?

grammar.title: Superlatives: the + -est / the most / the best
grammar.explanation_ar: للمقارنة بين ثلاثة أشياء أو أكثر نستخدم صيغة التفضيل: الصفات القصيرة تأخذ the + est (fresh → the freshest, old → the oldest). بعض الصفات شاذة: good → the best. ومع الأسماء: the most = الأكثر (the most meat).
grammar.explanation_en: To compare one thing with all the others, use the superlative: short adjectives take the + -est (fresh → the freshest, old → the oldest). Some are irregular: good → the best. With nouns use the most (the most meat).
examples: They have the freshest seafood in town.
It is the oldest outdoor seafood market in the United States.
The crabs here are the best.
The larger crabs have the most meat.
